root_idea.summary: A root centered on color, especially clear or pure whiteness, with extensions to animals characterized by whiteness or beauty and to several specialized lexical usages.
root_idea.development: The classical lexicon connects the color principle with the ewe and other female wild animals, prized or swift camels, fullness after eating, and smooth fertile land. These developments are broader root-level associations and are not all direct Qur'anic meanings of the attested form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular nominal citation form نَعْجَةٌ; the group also contains the Qur'anic plural نِعَاج.

senses.definition: A ewe; the female of the sheep.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Qur'anic usage, the singular نَعْجَة and plural نِعَاج refer to sheep females, including the contrasted flock and individual ewe in 38:23–24.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be of a clear or pure white colour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use describing clear whiteness in a person, thing, or colour.
Nominal or verbal-noun use for the quality of whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a clear or pure white colour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description; in the expression نِسَاءٌ نُعْجُ المَحَاجِرِ, it describes women whose areas around the eyes are clear white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fat and in good condition; to increase and become swollen or inflated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use for becoming plump or enlarged.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become heavy in the stomach after eating mutton.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic Form I use describing the digestive effect of eating sheep meat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel: to move swiftly or go with a particular pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I use describing a camel's speed or manner of travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a people's camels: to become fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV, in the construction أَنْعَجَ القَوْمُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The female of certain wild ruminants, including wild cattle, gazelles, and wild sheep; specifically a wild cow in نَعْجَةُ الرَّمْلِ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical usage distinct from the Qur'anic ewe sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel or she-camel of beautiful or white colouring, especially one that is prized or of generous race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied to camels; feminine نَاعِجَةٌ is used for a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swift, light, or active she-camel, including one used for hunting wild cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a she-camel's activity or use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman of beautiful complexion or colour.
Smooth, level land that is fertile and produces the shrub known as الرِّمْث.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَرْضٌ نَاعِجَةٌ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pure-white colour as a Form I verbal use.
Becoming fat, well-conditioned, swollen, or inflated.
Heaviness in the stomach after eating mutton.
A camel moving swiftly or at a particular pace.
Form IV use for camels becoming fat.
Illustrative expression applying the white-colour adjective to the area around women's eyes.
Repeats the mutton-related stomach heaviness use.
Qur'anic ewe sense and broader female-wild-animal branch.
Specific wild-cow use in نَعْجَةُ الرَّمْلِ.
Beautiful or prized camel branch and swift or active she-camel branch.

cautions: The public Qur'anic form is cited under singular نَعْجَةٌ, while the same QAC form group includes the inflected plural نِعَاج.
The broader Classical uses for wild animals, women, camels, and land are kept separate from the Qur'anic ewe sense.
